clue.text: Beg good bloke to translate jargon

indicators.note: translating something puts it into a new form, so these three words are rendered into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to coax a good fellow into putting technical talk into plain words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to translate' tells you to rearrange the letters of BEG GOOD BLOKE, all twelve of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbledegook is meaningless or overly technical language, a synonym for jargon.

clue.text: European has to shoot ancient incendiary

parts.note: a Greek is a European, a native of Greece
to shoot a gun is to fire it

explanation.surface: A European is obliged to open fire with some old explosive weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek fire was a burning liquid weapon used by the Byzantine navy, an incendiary of antiquity.

clue.text: Bishop overlooking a wicked act,… washing hands here?

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a sin is a wicked act

explanation.surface: A bishop turns a blind eye to some wickedness, perhaps then washing his hands of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' suggests ignoring, but in a down answer it means B is placed on top of A and SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is the bowl in which you wash your hands, so the question-marked phrase describes its use.

clue.text: Look to catch donkey with this?

definitions.text: Look to catch donkey with this?

indicators.note: one word catching another holds it inside

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A cowboy eyes a donkey and wonders whether this rope will catch it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' signals the container; read whole, the clue also describes what the rope is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a noosed rope thrown to catch animals, which the whole clue pictures.

clue.text: Her appearance is quite new

parts.note: a young woman making her first appearance in society, her coming-out being a novelty

explanation.surface: A remark that some woman looks very modern or fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman formally introduced into society for the first time, so her appearance there is new.

clue.text: Unexpectedly join the party

parts.note: to turn up at a gathering without having been invited

explanation.surface: Someone surprises everyone by becoming a member of a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to attend a party uninvited, arriving when not expected.

clue.text: No rag, perhaps, such a newspaper?

indicators.note: perhaps signals that these letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A question whether a respectable paper, certainly no rag, is a certain kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges NO and RAG; a rag is a disreputable newspaper, while this answer is a serious one.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or periodical that speaks for a party or group.

clue.text: Go secretly to play & win huge admiration

parts.note: to steal somewhere is to move stealthily
a play is a theatrical show, here the show

explanation.surface: Someone slips away quietly to a theatre production and is a huge success.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal the show is an idiom for outshining everyone else and winning the most praise.

clue.text: Rains heavily, as competitors in match heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is said aloud, giving one spelt differently

parts.note: the sides competing in a match are teams

explanation.surface: A downpour hits players while the game is on.
explanation.definitionFit: It teems when rain pours down heavily, a common idiom for a deluge.

clue.text: Shoe, old, damaged deliberately

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden shoe or clog
aged means old

explanation.surface: An old shoe has been purposely spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: Sabotage is said to come from workers throwing sabots into machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sabotaged has been wilfully damaged or wrecked.

clue.text: Learned man was not wrong to be detective's associate

parts.note: a doctor is a learned person holding a doctorate

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are put the wrong way round, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A scholar was right to become the partner of a sleuth.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor Watson is the friend and assistant of Sherlock Holmes in Conan Doyle's stories.

clue.text: Trying to establish a date

parts.note: reads like a historian fixing the year of something, but means inviting someone on a romantic outing

explanation.surface: A historian attempts to fix when something happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking out means inviting someone on a date, attempting to set one up.

clue.text: Study one chapter, a section of maths

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Read one chapter of a mathematics textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A conic is a conic section, the curve cut from a cone, studied in geometry.

clue.text: Might he sport barest min.?

indicators.note: a sport is a mutation, so these letters mutate into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether a certain man wears the scantiest clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' rearranges BAREST MIN; the whole clue pictures a scantily clad tribal man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribesman, member of a tribe, may be pictured wearing very little clothing.

clue.text: Caught up by seaweed, in the end

indicators.note: in places the seaweed inside the other word

parts.note: end as written
tangle is a type of kelp, a seaweed

explanation.surface: Someone eventually gets snared by seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. Tangle is a large brown kelp, a word met mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To be entangled is to be caught up or ensnared in something.

clue.text: In violent confusion, dis, patched to slammer

indicators.note: the page splits the word dispatched; something dispatched is sent off, so these letters are sent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is packed off to prison amid great turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text splits the anagram signal 'dispatched' as 'dis, patched'. 'In' is a link, and slammer is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a whirlpool, figuratively a state of violent turmoil.

clue.text: Friend of Spaniard, am I? Get away!

parts.note: taken as written
to go is to get away or leave

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are a Spaniard's friend, then dismisses the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, so it is what a Spaniard calls a friend.

clue.text: Humiliation in tidying mess

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the following word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Being made to clear up a mess is degrading.
explanation.walkthrough: IN stays as written; 'mess' rearranges TIDYING into DIGNITY.
explanation.definitionFit: An indignity is treatment causing shame or humiliation.

clue.text: Make big effort oneself to get coin away from specialist

indicators.note: taking something away from a word removes those letters

parts.note: an expert is a specialist
P is short for penny, a coin

explanation.surface: Someone works hard to win money off an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes P (penny) from EXPERT. The definition reads as 'exert oneself'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert oneself is to make a great effort or strive hard.

clue.text: Cosmetic watchdog?

definitions.meaning: make-up coloured powder applied to the lids
humorously, an observer who keeps an eye on someone by tailing them

explanation.surface: A make-up product is called a guard dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye shadow is a cosmetic for the eyelids; read as eye plus shadow, it is someone who watches and follows.

clue.text: Admirable chap to name bird

parts.note: a hero is an admirable man

explanation.surface: A fine fellow is asked to identify a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Letter from abroad about popular animal

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A foreign letter mentions a well-loved creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter from abroad' looks like post; it is a foreign alphabet's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhino, short for rhinoceros, is a large horned animal.

clue.text: It draws attention to insult about fat belly

indicators.note: about means around, so the insult goes round the belly

parts.note: a slight is an insult or snub
a pot or pot belly is a fat stomach

explanation.surface: Someone is rude about another's paunch, which gets noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotlight is a lamp that focuses attention on someone, and figuratively public attention itself.

clue.text: Love to exercise soldiers-that's Falstaff, for one

parts.note: O is zero, love in tennis scoring
PE is physical education, exercise
RA is the Royal Artillery, soldiers

explanation.surface: Romance, then drill for troops, as Shakespeare's fat knight might enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff looks like Shakespeare's character but here is Verdi's last work.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff is an opera by Verdi, so it is an example of the form.

clue.text: It's plain all's up with a number

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: all, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A simple statement that everything is finished with a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ALL into LLA, with NO below.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad grassy plain in South America.

clue.text: Court document's bulky, that's obvious

parts.note: a writ is a document issued by a court
large means bulky

explanation.surface: A thick legal paper makes its point clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Writ large is an idiom meaning clearly obvious or magnified.

clue.text: A minor shortfall of such acid in body

indicators.note: a shortfall leaves the word short, so its final letter falls away

explanation.surface: A small deficiency of some acid in the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortfall' drops the last letter R of MINOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins in the body.

clue.text: You wouldn't expect the Telegraph to be so highly critical

definitions.text: You wouldn't expect the Telegraph to be so
definitions.meaning: a Conservative-leaning paper would not criticise a party member

explanation.surface: The Telegraph is not usually so harsh in its judgments.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is a British newspaper that traditionally supports the Conservative Party, whose members are called Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Condemnatory means expressing strong disapproval, so highly critical is a synonym.
